title: Culture gains a stronger name and place in the European Parliament’s Horizon Europe compromise
content:
The Name Place Fund coalition, which brings together culture and research organisations advocating for stronger support for culture in Horizon Europe and the European Competitiveness Fund, welcomes the cross-party compromise text on Horizon Europe 2028-2034 negotiated in the European Parliament. 

It was prepared by rapporteurs Christian Ehler (EPP) and René Repasi (S&D) together with the shadow rapporteurs. The compromise is scheduled for a vote in Parliament’s Industry, Research and Energy (ITRE) Committee on 10 November. This text will be the starting point for the Parliament’s negotiations with the Commission and the Council. 

After long negotiations, culture, creativity and artistic research finally have a more prominent place in the future EU research and innovation programme, signalling an important shift in how the role of arts and culture in research and innovation is understood.

title: Webinar – Fighting Trafficking of Cultural Property: Art Market and Civil Society at the Helm
content:
Even if the project has officially ended, the partners of ANCHISE are still active!

Join our next webinar, an extended edition of ANCHISE Talks, organised by Michael Culture Association and our partner ENCATC, in collaboration with Blue Shield – Illegal Trafficking Working Group.       

13 November 2026 | 16:30–18:00 CET – Online

Registration: here

13 November 2026 | 16:30–18:00 CET – Online

Registration: here

To celebrate (one day in advance) the UNESCO International Day against Illicit Trafficking in Cultural Property, we will discuss two parallel topics important for our sector:

  • UNESCO’s revised International Code of Ethics for Traders in Cultural Property. What are its main principles, and how can they translate into practice?  How can civil society organisations contribute to strengthening these efforts? Louise Malecot and Marie-José Minone (UNESCO) will present the revised Code and its implications, followed by Dr. Nancy Von Breska (Senior Cultural Heritage Expert, Lapislazul), who will address its practical implementation in the art market together with the audience.
